cases.prompt: Which LLM should we use for our claims-summary assistant?
expected: Asks once for the candidate shortlist with the team's own eval scores, prices and latency (dated, sourced) and for the criteria and hard constraints
Offers assets/candidates-template.csv and assets/criteria-template.csv; does not quote any model price, benchmark score or capability from memory

cases.prompt: Rank these five candidates on our criteria and workload and tell me which model to pick.
expected: Runs scripts/select_model.py; eliminates Cedar-8 and Delta-Pro with reasons; Atlas-L wins at 0.6 with Birch-70 runner-up; sensitivity stable

cases.prompt: Pick a model for us using these criteria.
expected: Asks for the candidates file instead of inventing a shortlist or model facts

cases.prompt: We must self-host and need at least 0.85 task accuracy. Which model?
expected: Every candidate is eliminated with reasons; the run exits 1 and decision.md says no candidate meets the hard constraints instead of recommending one anyway

checks.check: contains:"None of the 5 candidates survives the hard constraints"

cases.prompt: Rank on cost too, but I don't have volumes yet.
expected: Refuses to compute monthly cost without a workload; exits with an input error rather than assuming volumes

cases.prompt: We run Delta-Pro in production today. Re-rank the candidates on our criteria and tell me whether to switch.
expected: Shows the incumbent Delta-Pro fails the 2,500 ms p95 latency hard constraint, recommends switching to Atlas-L, saves 2,140.00 USD a month at the workload, and notes task accuracy is the one criterion where the incumbent is better

checks.check: contains:"eliminated by the hard constraints (p95_latency_ms = 3000 above hard_max 2500)"
